name: Learn: RuntimeClass (sandboxing)
objective: CKS › Minimize Microservice Vulnerabilities (20%). Goal: use RuntimeClass to select a sandboxed container runtime (e.g. gVisor/runsc or Kata) for sensitive workloads, and combine it with capability-dropping + non-root hardening — the microservice-isolation tasks that appear on the CKS.
description: Learn how RuntimeClass lets you run sensitive pods on a stronger-isolation runtime (a gVisor or Kata sandbox) instead of the default runc, step by step — then layer capability-dropping and non-root on top for defence in depth.

questions.title: Create a RuntimeClass
questions.teach:
A **RuntimeClass** (`apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1`, `kind: RuntimeClass`) is a **cluster-scoped** object that names a container runtime the kubelet can use. Its required **`handler`** is a string the node's CRI maps to a runtime binary — e.g. gVisor's `runsc`.

**Gotcha:** `handler` is a **top-level** field, NOT under `spec` (there is no `spec`) — nesting it is a classic trap.
questions.prompt:
Create a cluster-scoped RuntimeClass named `gvisor` whose `handler` is `runsc`.

Target: `kubectl get runtimeclass gvisor` exists and its `.handler` is `runsc`.
questions.hint: RuntimeClass is `apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1`, `kind: RuntimeClass`, with `metadata.name` and a top-level `handler:` field (handler is NOT under spec). Apply it with `kubectl apply -f -`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1
kind: RuntimeClass
metadata:
  name: gvisor
handler: runsc
YAML
kubectl get runtimeclass gvisor -o jsonpath='{.handler}'   # runsc

questions.title: Run a pod on that RuntimeClass
questions.teach:
A pod opts into a RuntimeClass via **`spec.runtimeClassName: <name>`** — a pod-level field. `kubectl run` has no flag for it, so inject it with `--overrides='{"spec":{"runtimeClassName":"gvisor"}}'`.

**Gotcha:** `runsc` isn't installed here, so the pod stays Pending — that's expected; we only grade the spec field, not that it ran.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `runtimeclass-learn`, create a pod named `sandboxed` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) that requests the `gvisor` RuntimeClass via `spec.runtimeClassName`.

Target: pod `sandboxed` has `.spec.runtimeClassName` = `gvisor`. (Do NOT expect it to be Running — the runsc handler is absent on this node.)
questions.hint: `kubectl run` supports `--overrides` to inject arbitrary spec fields: `--overrides='{"spec":{"runtimeClassName":"gvisor"}}'`. Or write the pod YAML with `spec.runtimeClassName: gvisor`.
questions.solution:
kubectl run sandboxed -n runtimeclass-learn --image=busybox:1.36 --overrides='{"spec":{"runtimeClassName":"gvisor"}}' --command -- sleep 3600
kubectl get pod sandboxed -n runtimeclass-learn -o jsonpath='{.spec.runtimeClassName}'   # gvisor

questions.title: Contrast with an un-sandboxed pod
questions.teach:
RuntimeClass lets you pick isolation **per workload**: sandbox the sensitive pods, leave the rest on the default. A pod with **no `runtimeClassName`** runs on the node's default runtime (usually `runc`), sharing the host kernel directly. **Gotcha:** `kubectl get pod

-o jsonpath='{.spec.runtimeClassName}'` returns empty for a default-runtime pod — that empty string is the expected "normal" state.
questions.prompt:
In `runtimeclass-learn`, create a second pod named `normal` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) with **no** `runtimeClassName` (default runtime).

Target: `sandboxed`'s `.spec.runtimeClassName` is `gvisor` while `normal`'s is empty — the two differ.
questions.hint: Just `kubectl run normal -n runtimeclass-learn --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600` (no overrides). Leaving runtimeClassName unset means the default runtime.
questions.solution:
kubectl run normal -n runtimeclass-learn --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600
kubectl get pod normal    -n runtimeclass-learn -o jsonpath='{.spec.runtimeClassName}'   # (empty)
kubectl get pod sandboxed -n runtimeclass-learn -o jsonpath='{.spec.runtimeClassName}'   # gvisor

verification.description: 'sandboxed' uses gvisor, 'normal' uses the default runtime (they differ)

questions.title: Harden the sandboxed pod (defence in depth)
questions.teach:
A sandbox is one layer — stack **securityContext** hardening for defence in depth. Here: **drop ALL capabilities** (`securityContext.capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`) and **run non-root** (`runAsNonRoot: true` + `runAsUser: 1000`).

**Gotcha:** `capabilities` is a **container-level** field — setting it pod-level is a silent no-op. Keep `spec.runtimeClassName: gvisor` when you recreate the pod to harden it.
questions.prompt:
Replace pod `sandboxed` in `runtimeclass-learn` so it still requests `runtimeClassName: gvisor` AND its container drops **ALL** capabilities and runs non-root (`runAsNonRoot: true`, `runAsUser: 1000`). Keep image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`.

Target: pod `sandboxed` has runtimeClassName `gvisor`, `runAsNonRoot: true`, and its container's `capabilities.drop` contains `ALL`.
questions.hint: Delete and recreate with a YAML that has `spec.runtimeClassName: gvisor`, `spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true` + `runAsUser: 1000`, and the container's `securityContext.capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`. busybox sleep runs fine as uid 1000.
questions.solution:
kubectl delete pod sandboxed -n runtimeclass-learn --ignore-not-found
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sandboxed
  namespace: runtimeclass-learn
spec:
  runtimeClassName: gvisor
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 1000
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    securityContext:
      capabilities:
        drop: ["ALL"]
YAML

verification.description: 'sandboxed' keeps gvisor AND drops ALL caps + runs non-root

questions.title: Offer a second runtime (Kata)
questions.teach:
A cluster can expose **several** RuntimeClasses so workloads pick the isolation they need — e.g. `gvisor` (handler `runsc`) alongside `kata` (handler `kata`) for micro-VM isolation. They coexist independently; `kubectl get runtimeclass` lists them all.

**Gotcha:** the class **name** (what pods reference) and the **`handler`** (what the CRI maps to a binary) are separate fields — here `kata`'s name and handler happen to match, but don't conflate them.
questions.prompt:
Create a second RuntimeClass named `kata` whose `handler` is `kata`.

Target: `kubectl get runtimeclass` lists both `gvisor` and `kata`, and `kata`'s `.handler` is `kata`.
questions.hint: Same shape as step 1: `apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1`, `kind: RuntimeClass`, `metadata.name: kata`, top-level `handler: kata`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1
kind: RuntimeClass
metadata:
  name: kata
handler: kata
YAML
kubectl get runtimeclass   # gvisor + kata
